 SOUTH CAROLINA (WPDE) — South Carolina ranks as the second least affordable state for student loan payments , according to a new national analysis highlighting the financial challenges borrowers face.
 Student Choice, a credit union student loan marketplace, recently released its Student Loan Affordability Index, which compares student loan payments, income, delinquency rates and living costs across all 50 states.
 According to the report, South Carolina borrowers pay an estimate of $433 a month toward student loans, slightly above the national average of $419.
 Those payments account for 8.2% of the state's per capita income, the fourth-highest share in the country.
 The report also found that South Carolina has the nation's fourth-highest student loan delinquency rate, with 11.1% of outstanding loan balances at least 90 days past due, compared with nearly 10% nationally.
 More than 746,000 South Carolina residents carry federal student loan debt, totaling approximately $29.1 billion. The average outstanding balance per borrower is $38,992.

 Mississippi was the only state ranked less affordable than South Carolina, followed by Georgia, Alabama and Hawaii, which rounded out the five least affordable states.
 The findings highlight the financial challenges borrowers face as they balance student loan payments with everyday expenses, including housing and other household costs.
 The report also emphasizes the importance of understanding borrowing costs and repayment obligations before taking out student loans.
